summary: Steve Grothoff walks through Romans 12:1-2 to ask what true, acceptable worship actually looks like -- and how we drift into worship God never asked for. He traces real biblical examples of unacceptable worship (worshiping false gods, worshiping the true God in a selfstyled way instead of His way, and going through religious motions with a false heart) before showing that acceptable worship flows from a mind renewed by God, not conformity to the world. The sermon closes by widening worship beyond Sunday singing into a whole-life pattern: obedience, love, generosity, discipleship, testimony, and gathering with the church.
takeaways: Worship means presenting our whole lives to God as a living sacrifice (Romans 12:1), not just something we do on Sunday morning.
Scripture shows real patterns of unacceptable worship: worshiping false gods, worshiping the true God our own way instead of His way, and empty ritual from a false heart.
Acceptable worship comes from being transformed by a renewed mind, not from being conformed to the world (Romans 12:2).
Practical worship includes love, obedience, generosity, teaching and discipling others, sharing our testimony, and gathering with the church -- not singing alone.
The sermon closes with an invitation to fully surrender to Christ as the truest act of worship.
